manuscripts.title: Hilbert’s tenth problem over the rational numbers

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: There is no algorithm which, given a polynomial f ∈ Z[X1, . . . , Xn], with n part of the input, decides whether f has a zero in Qn.

For each occurrence of a prime r in this list and each of the two places vr of F above it, there are nonzero integers h, j0, chosen independently of a ∈ Z, such that every a ∈ Z satisfies conditions (i) and (ii) of Lemma 2.3 in the ordinary setting: take R = Z, its identity embedding in the ordinary structure, Ta = aP, q = r, and v∗ = vr, normalized by vr(r) = 1. candidates.label: Corollary 7.1
candidates.heading: Corollary 7.1.
candidates.statement: With the usual effective coding, let H10(Q) be the set of integral polynomials having a rational zero, with the number of variables part of the input. Then H10(Q) has Turing degree 0′, the degree of the halting problem. The same is true for each of the following restricted input problems: (i) rational solvability for integral polynomials of total degree at most four; (ii) given a nonempty finite list q1, . . . , qs ∈ Z[X1, . . . , XN ], each of total degree at most two, whether Ps i=1 q2 i has a zero in QN . No bound is imposed on the number of variables, the number of summands in (ii), or the coefficient heights.

candidates.heading: Theorem 4.14 (The limit and evaluation interface).
candidates.statement: For the ring data fixed at the start of this section, retain the finite target-side arithmetic diagrams with their maps to original cochains, homotopies, and dualities as in Lemma 4.4. The moving characters, local conditions, and evaluation constructions then have the following simultaneous properties: 1. Every specified finite target-side arithmetic diagram admits a bounded free model together with maps to its original cochains; the specified maps, homotopies and dualities survive the inner limit. 2. At the stated height-one tests the relaxed active local complexes are acyclic, and the Selmer duality pairs degrees one and two. The residual sizes needed for the outer construction are bounded independently of the active conductor support, with dependence only on E, the bound on ω(disc K), and the number of retained derivative primes. 4. Inner and outer H1 are detected by actual crossed cocycles, including on the exact common kernel. The evaluations and their degree-two identities can be realized by finite Chebotarev conditions without disturbing earlier finite data. These assertions do not assert an Euler-system reciprocity law or an integral derivative class that has not first been constructed at finite level. candidates.statement: Under the arithmetic lower bounds in Lemma 7.5, the symbols of either coefficient source have the following properties. 1. The replacement has the product labels at all retained places. Its coefficient system has support S ∪ (U \ {p}): the entire rational prime p, including both places above it when it splits in F, is omitted. 3. A split vertex with trivial label in the elementary extension for the other vertices has zero symbol. 4. candidates.label: Theorem 8.3
candidates.name: Address lemma
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.3 (Address lemma).
candidates.statement: Suppose the binary symbols under consideration depend only on the arithmetic graph data and satisfy the contraction, whole-rational-prime omission, and primary-isolation rules of Proposition 7.9, with the realization freedoms of Lemma 8.1. Contraction includes the product labels and external incidences, and the zero rule for two simple vertices. These identities are required only on nonempty configurations and for contractions with nonempty output. Fix b ≥ 1 and either of the following terminal arrangements. 1. One symbol, a nonempty set of always active terminals, and a nonzero polynomial in their independent pair bits. 2. One or two symbols on terminals with nonzero linear activations, including at least one terminal for every nonzero linear form. At each x ̸= 0 each symbol separately is a nonzero polynomial in the active terminal bits. The symbols may read different compatible projections of a common graph alphabet and may have fixed stationary external data. Suppose also that at each nonzero address the total active terminal data, together with any stationary external data, obey the required filter. Starting from any fixed realization of the 68 terminal and stationary vertices, one can adjoin finitely many fresh primary auxiliary vertices, activated by nonzero linear forms, and choose only incidences involving these new vertices so that every symbol equals 1 at every x ̸= 0. All data on the original vertices remain unchanged. No auxiliary is present at 0. All auxiliaries may satisfy the fixed splitting and neutral external-incidence conditions incorporated into the primary type. It is enough that a terminal polynomial have a nonzero evaluation or a nonzero iterated edge difference. In particular a partitionability certificate suffices for the stationary hypothesis.

candidates.statement: The following statements hold for the fixed curve and fixed local data. 1. If arbitrarily large binary cubes based at h0, with no old prime removed, have nonzero central values at every other address and satisfy v(L∗(hx)) − 2w(hx) − s(hx) ≤ B (x ̸= 0), then the base central value is nonzero and satisfies the same inequality with B replaced by B + C. The constant C depends only on the fixed curve and local data, not on h0, its number of prime factors, or the cube dimension. The dimension required for the argument may depend on the base. The cyclotomic lower bound at an analytically nonvanishing parameter is also available. 2. Corollary 4.1 has the following uniform form. If k < 0 is an odd fundamental discrimi- nant with at most A prime factors, K = Q( √ k) is neither an extra-unit field nor the CM field, k is a square at 2Nh, and the twists h, hk have respective analytic orders one and zero, then their ring-class Heegner sum has free-line index jh(k) satisfying 2jh(k) ≥ 4w(h) + s(h) + s(hk) − CE,A. (9.1) For a fixed such k, Theorem 4.2 applies to cubes based at h = 1 whose new primes all split in K. If s2(E/K) = 1 and the nonzero addresses have product analytic order one and uniformly bounded 2jh(k) − 4w(h) − s(h) − s(hk), the base product has analytic order one. 3. The even coefficient system, exact same-filter square comparison, divided operators, and trace identities of Proposition 7.1 and Lemmas 7.6, 7.7, and 7.8 are available. After a uniform lower bound for the relevant point indices has been proved, the moving odd coefficient system and its stabilized minimum are available as in Proposition 7.4 and Lemma 7.5. The resulting unit symbols satisfy the contraction, good-twin, and primary-isolation rules of Proposition 7.9. An even unit gives L∗(h) ̸= 0, v(L∗(h)) ≤ 2w(h) + C; (9.2) an odd unit gives analytic order one and j(Ph) ≤ w(h) + C. (9.3) The constants are independent of the number and sizes of the variable primes. The fixed genus partner used to define Ph is denoted h∗. 4. Arithmetic realization and the forest and address statements of Lemmas 8.1 and 8.4 and Theorem 8.3 hold. In particular, separate nonzero terminal polynomials may be addressed simultaneously. Primary auxiliaries preserve all fixed local classes, have neutral incidence to specified stationary external vertices, and may be required to split in any compatible fixed fields. They contribute no prime at address zero.

manuscripts.title: Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.name: The 2-converse
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1 (The 2-converse).
candidates.statement: For every elliptic curve E/Q with c2(E) ∈ {0, 1}, a(E) = r(E) = c2(E), Sha(E/Q) is finite.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.name: Goldfeld’s analytic density conjecture
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2 (Goldfeld’s analytic density conjecture).
candidates.statement: For every elliptic curve E/Q and each j ∈ {0, 1}, lim X→∞ #{d ∈ D(X) : a(E(d)) = j} #D(X) = 1 2 . Consequently the twists of analytic rank at least two have density zero. For a density-one set of signed squarefree parameters d, the analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks of E(d) agree and its whole Tate–Shafarevich group is finite.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.3

candidates.heading: Corollary 1.3 (A finite Selmer criterion).
candidates.statement: If d2(E) ∈ {0, 1}, then a(E) = r(E) = c2(E) = d2(E), Sha(E/Q) is finite, Sha(E/Q)[2∞ ] = 0.

(3.4) Then L(E(h0), 1) ̸= 0 and D(h0) ≤ B + CE. (3.5) The necessary dimension may depend on h0, its finite Selmer group, and the bound in Equation (3.4); CE does not.

(ii) If ε = −1, they can be chosen with L′(E(D), 1) ̸= 0, so the central zero is simple. The bound five in (i) is independent of E, S, B and the prescribed classes. candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Insertion of a pair of simple primes).
candidates.statement: Suppose E(Q)[2] ̸= 0 and U has matching parity. Let a rational elementary label, relative to S and all existing split vertices, be realized by a simple prime q with #E(Fq) ≡ 2 (mod 4). Inserting two fresh simple primes with this same label leaves A(U) unchanged. Their mutual simple-edge label, and their labels against other simple vertices, do not affect this assertion.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.8
candidates.name: Irreducible substitution rules
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.8 (Irreducible substitution rules).
candidates.statement: Suppose E[2] is irreducible. (i) On matching BU , coefficient 1 of a product of root traces reads A on the union of U and those roots. It depends on the roots only through their total rational elementary label relative to S ∪ U. Any finite collection of roots, including the empty collection, may be replaced in this test by one virtual root with that label. (ii) Changing the Legendre bit of that root against a split vertex p has additive derivative equal to deletion of p, with its rational labels away from p transferred to the total root label. Changing the root bit against a simple vertex has derivative zero. 33 (iii) To vary a simple vertex q, omit it and use opposite BV , retaining the other root probes. At another simple vertex p, choose Frobenius lifts g and ϕp for q and p. If their transposition images are different, the derivative under g 7→ gτp deletes both p and q and transfers their rational labels to the root total. If their transposition images are equal, the derivative is zero. (iv) In the test in (iii), variation at a split p is given by the first-shell factors cp times symbols of merged configurations whose weight is one less. It consequently vanishes whenever all symbols of that lower weight vanish. All these assertions preserve every specified label at the other vertices, and use the chosen place for inertia and Frobenius.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.10
candidates.name: Symbol rules
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.10 (Symbol rules).
candidates.statement: For either coefficient source of Propositions 4.1 and 4.2, assume its stated coefficient lower bound and use its normalized symbol and filter. Then the following rules hold for finite configurations of primes outside the level support. (i) With rational two-torsion, the elementary-label factorizations, contraction except in the simple–simple case, and isolation by a trivial split label are those of Proposition 5.5. A pair of identical simple labels realized with #E(Fq)/2 odd can be inserted without changing the symbol, as in Proposition 5.6. (ii) With irreducible E[2], all root probes combine into one total rational elementary label. A root-bit derivative at a split vertex deletes that vertex, while at a simple vertex it is zero. The derivative between two simple vertices deletes both when their transposition images are different, and is zero when they are equal. The remaining simple–split shell has weight one less. These are the rules of Proposition 5.8. (iii) At the least weight supporting a nonzero symbol in the irreducible case, each nonroot may be moved with only its fixed-support elementary Frobenius label prescribed; internal edges impose no further condition on the value, subject to matching the total root label. This is Lemma 5.9. The analytic and finite-Selmer consequences of a nonzero symbol remain those of Proposi- tion 4.4. In the odd source the rules mean finite tests at arbitrarily high stages chosen in the ultrafilter-large sets of the prescribed stabilization.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.6

candidates.heading: Theorem 6.6 (Address lemma).
candidates.statement: Assume the contraction, isolation, and whole-prime omission rules of Proposition 5.5, or the same rules for another symbol, together with the realization freedoms of Lemma 6.1. Let b ≥ 1 and consider either of the following terminal arrangements: 1. One symbol on a nonempty set of always active terminals, whose polynomial in the independent pair bits is nonzero. 2. One or two symbols on terminals with nonzero linear activations, including a terminal for every nonzero linear form. At each x ̸= 0, each symbol separately is a nonzero polynomial in the active bits. The symbols may have stationary external data and may read compatible projections of a common graph. At every x ̸= 0, assume that the active terminal data and the stationary external data obey each required filter. Then finitely many primary auxiliaries with nonzero linear activations, and one realizable assignment of graph bits, make all the symbols 1 at every x ̸= 0. No auxiliary is present at 0. All may satisfy fixed splitting and neutral-incidence conditions included in their primary type. A nonzero evaluation or a nonzero iterated edge difference suffices for the polynomial hypothesis. In particular, a partition as in Definition 6.2 suffices in the stationary case.

candidates.heading: Proposition 7.5 (Partitionable even estimate).

candidates.heading: Proposition 9.5 (An odd cube with a bounded even companion).
candidates.statement: For the fixed symbols A, A0 just chosen, suppose A(1) = 0. candidates.heading: Proposition 13.16 (Integral evaluation through the outer limit).
candidates.statement: Let Cj be any family of the preceding limiting complexes, completed over Oj = d Λ(2), possibly for different quadratic fields Kj. Suppose their minimal ranks are bounded. candidates.heading: Theorem 13.19 (Compatibility of the limit constructions).

manuscripts.title: Reconstruction of Function Fields from Mod-ℓ Milnor K-Theory

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let ℓ be any prime. Let K/k and L/l be finitely generated extensions of arbitrary algebraically closed fields, with char k, char l ̸= ℓ and trdeg(K/k), trdeg(L/l) ≥ 2. Then (1.1) is bijective. In particular, a compatible isomorphism VK → VL forces equality of the characteristics and of the relative transcendence degrees.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.1
candidates.name: Alternating-pair valuation theory
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.1 (Alternating-pair valuation theory).
candidates.statement: Let F be a field and set A± F = {f ∈ AF : f(−1) = 0}. (i) Every valuative subset Σ ⊂ AF has a unique coarsest valuation vΣ with Σ ⊂ IvΣ . In particular, vΣ coarsens every valuation whose inertia contains Σ. For such a valuation w, this coarsening is obtained by quotienting wF by its largest convex subgroup contained in w( T f∈Σ ker f). 5 (ii) If S ⊂ A± F is an alternating linear subspace, its valuative elements form a valuative sub- space S0 of codimension at most one. Moreover S ⊂ DvS0 . (iii) If Σ ⊂ A± F is valuative and g ∈ A± F is alternating with every element of Σ, then g ∈ DvΣ .

candidates.heading: Proposition 2.6.
candidates.statement: The maximum dimension of an alternating subspace of AF is s. If S ⊂ AF is alternating of dimension s, and v is the valuation associated to its valuative part S0, then S0 = Iv and equality holds in (2.2) for v.

candidates.heading: Proposition 2.7.
candidates.statement: Assume s ≥ 2. A line H ⊂ AF is the inertia of a quasi-divisorial valuation if and only if H = S1 ∩ S2 for alternating subspaces S1, S2 ⊂ AF of dimension s. (2.6) The quasi-divisorial valuation v with Iv = H is unique. For any nonzero h ∈ H, its decomposition space is Dv = {g ∈ AF : (h, g) is alternating}. (2.7)

candidates.heading: Corollary 2.9.
candidates.statement: For the fields K/k, L/l of Theorem 1.1, a compatible isomorphism Θ forces trdeg(K/k) = trdeg(L/l) = d, say. Its dual Φ matches the inertia–decomposition pairs of quasi- prime divisors, and, successively, the pairs of quasi-prime r-divisors for 1 ≤ r ≤ d − 1. For a matched pair of valuations v on K and w on L, it induces a topological linear isomorphism ALw ∼ − − → AKv preserving alternating pairs in both directions.

Then b Jv contains the full minimized inertia group b Iu of every c.r. quasi-prime divisor u of Fv/κv.

candidates.name: Positive-density congruence subgroup property
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Positive-density congruence subgroup property).
candidates.statement: Let k be a number field and G an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic k-group. Let M/k be the minimal Galois extension over which G becomes an inner form of the split group, and let Spl(M/k) be the set of nonarchimedean places of k that split completely in M. Suppose that S is a set of places of k which contains all archimedean places, contains no nonarchimedean place v with rankkv G = 0, and satisfies dk S ∩ Spl(M/k)  > 0, where dk denotes Dirichlet density and the indicated density is assumed to exist. Then the S- congruence kernel is trivial: CS (G) = {1}. Equivalently, for any fixed faithful k-defined representation of G, the associated group G(O(S)) over the ring of S-integers has the classical congruence subgroup property: every finite-index normal subgroup contains a principal congruence subgroup of some nonzero ideal level.

Then R has finite index, P0 is open and normal in GA, and V is finite. For every positive-rank nonarchimedean place w, the closure of R in the adelic product away from w is exactly the inverse image of P0. To prove (MP) for G, it suffices to show V = 1 for every e. If γ ∈ V0, representatives of γR can be chosen arbitrarily close to 1 at any prescribed finite set of places. Away from A, these near-identity conditions may be replaced by arbitrary nonempty local open conditions. Finitely many nonempty Zariski open conditions may be imposed simultaneously.

candidates.heading: Proposition 2.6 (Power-factor approximation).
candidates.statement: Let G be k-anisotropic, with P, η, R, and X = x∗G as above. Fix γ ∈ G(k), the rational coset C = x∗γR ⊂ X(k), a geometrically codimension-at- least-two closed subset D ⊂ X, and a finite set B containing the archimedean places, A, and the exceptions for fixed integral models and sufficiently small residue fields. Include in B a positive-rank finite place v0. At B prescribe nonempty local open conditions compatible with the closure of C in Proposition 2.3. At each finite place outside B, prescribe an allowed set Uv ⊂ X(kv). Assume: (i) every integral point whose reduction avoids D belongs to Uv; (ii) Uv contains a nonempty local open set; (iii) single-pole configurations are tested by finitely many algebraic nonvanishing conditions over P, independent of v. Their nonemptiness is compatible with the following order of choices. First choose at least two disjoint basic lists, with their conjugator tuple in a nonempty Zariski open subset of its product of copies of G. For each such tuple there is a nonempty Zariski open subset of X in which to choose x. After x is fixed, for every finite number of additional factors there is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the corresponding product of copies of G in which to choose their conjugators. For every tuple allowed by these successive choices, the tests restrict to a nonempty open subset of each absolute boundary hyperplane away from the others. They guarantee membership in Uv at a single-pole reduction, outside finitely many model exceptions for the fixed data. In the third condition the tests are imposed with all their Galois conjugates. Appending additional factors is required to preserve the tests on an existing hyperplane when the new parameters are set to 1. Thus their insertion does not remove the previously available open subsets. The additional factors permit the local moves required by the second condition. Then there is x′ ∈ C satisfying the prescribed conditions at B and belonging to Uv for every finite v / ∈ B. Finitely many nonempty Zariski open conditions on the initial representative and conjugators can be included in their choice, provided they are compatible with the third condition.

The construction preserves current-core equivariance, the cell spans and padding stated in (5.5) and the paragraph following it, all inherited accounting classes without splitting, and the property that one new cell meets at most one surviving old cell of each old child. After clipping, the raw cap per cell and remaining mask is N0. It supports the coarsening rule of Proposition 5.3 at each subsequent sparse step. Aside from the cap clipping separately bounded by (5.10), its total first-mass loss can be made arbitrarily small relative to the selected block mass by the fixed parameter cutoffs. An expected loss bound over the specified finite partition jitters suffices; the structural assertions and core equivariance hold for every realized construction. The comparison bounds apply to the actual running tables or to the nonnegative majorants indicated in their proofs.

candidates.heading: Proposition 5.7 (Virtual product marginals).
candidates.statement: For each retained good row, there is a nonnegative virtual weight on its true numerator grid with the following properties. 1. It dominates the actual final weight, and its first mass lies between chardϕ(v)r(v) and ϕ(v)r(v). 2. Its total excess over the actual final first mass is exactly accounted for by the first-moment discard losses in the projected tables, when the virtual weight omits the soft and additional static tests, cap clipping, and partition discards. 3. At fixed static anchor choices, every subset of the actual hard and adaptive fields has mean equal to the product of its local means. An actual hard field has mean 1 − bp/p when it forbids bp ≤ 2 distinct residues, or mean Rp when it is a prescribed scalar; adaptive full fields have mean Rp. For upper counts one may retain just one hard birth exclusion at each applicable prime, or the scalar Rp when there is no exclusion. Any subset of the resulting hard and adaptive fields has the product of its ordinary local means. 4. Fields through a prime p, restricted to a later projection of denominator v′, have a joint period dividing v′ of size at most exp(O(p)). Domination in the first item is after the static anchor average; it is not required separately for each auxiliary anchor choice.

candidates.heading: Corollary 8.4 (Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties).
candidates.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed field and A/K an abelian variety of dimension g. For every prime ℓ ̸= char(K), numerical and ℓ-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on A. At each iteration choose such compatible represen- tatives and equip the new base with the stable inf-multiplicity orbifold structure of the composite. There is a finite sequence of ordinary J-negative steps over V , all projective over V , whose last adjoint is curve-nef over V , meaning that it has nonnegative degree on every curve contracted over V . Every working space is compact Kähler and globally strongly Q-factorial. On a common resolution the comparison from the first adjoint to the last is effective and exceptional over the last space.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.5
candidates.name: Small strong models
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.5 (Small strong models).
candidates.statement: Let (S, ∆) be an effective rational dlt pair on a normal compact Kähler space, with rational-line adjoint. Suppose that an effective rational Cartier divisor D satisfies Supp D = Supp⌊∆⌋. There is a projective small morphism h : Y → S, with Y globally strongly Q-factorial and compact Kähler, which is crepant for the full adjoint and is an isomorphism over the smooth locus of S. The transformed full pair is dlt. The same assertion for an ordinary klt pair allows D = 0.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.8
candidates.name: Contracting a known negative part
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.8 (Contracting a known negative part).
candidates.statement: Let (T, B) be an effective rational dlt pair on a globally strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler space, and put J = KT + B. Suppose there is an actual rational-line identity J ∼Q P + E, where P is analytically nef, E is an effective rational Cartier divisor, and, on one smooth compact Kähler resolution π : W → T projective over T, N(π∗ {J}) = π∗ E. There is a finite ordinary J-negative program to a nef model T′ which contracts precisely the prime components of E among the primes of T. Every step is P-trivial, with a fixed Cartier exponent as in Lemma 3.6, and JT′ ∼Q PT′ . If P is semiample, then so is this actual last adjoint.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.10
candidates.name: Terminal models in Kodaira dimension zero
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.10 (Terminal models in Kodaira dimension zero).
candidates.statement: Let X be a smooth compact Kähler d-fold with d < n and κ(X, KX) = 0. A finite ordinary KX-negative program reaches a globally strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler terminal space Xmin whose actual canonical rational line is torsion. For every smooth compact Kähler resolution projective over Xmin, the decompositions in Equations (3.3) and (3.4) hold.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.13
candidates.name: Special termination for a chosen dlt scaling
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.13 (Special termination for a chosen dlt scaling).
candidates.statement: Assume Gd for every d < n. Let (X, B) be an effective rational dlt pair on a smooth compact Kähler n-fold, and suppose L = KX +B is pseudo-effective. There is a Kähler scaling direction ω, with {L} + ω Kähler, and a scaling as in Lemma 3.6, such that after finitely many steps the exceptional, flipping, and flipped loci are disjoint from the reduced floors of the working pairs.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.14
candidates.name: A signed adjoint supported on the floor
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.14 (A signed adjoint supported on the floor).
candidates.statement: Assume Gd for every d < n. In the situation of Theorem 3.13, suppose moreover that L is rationally linearly equivalent, as an actual rational line, to a signed rational divisor supported on ⌊B⌋. The scaling can be chosen to reach a nef ordinary dlt model after finitely many steps.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.18
candidates.name: A global algebra for a detected flip
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.18 (A global algebra for a detected flip).
candidates.statement: Let (T, B + M) be a gklt pair on a normal compact Kähler space which is globally strongly Q-factorial, and let A ∈ H1,1 BC(T, R) be its adjoint class. Let f : T → Z be a projective small contraction onto a normal compact Kähler space. Suppose that the classes of all f-vertical curves lie on one ray R ⊂ NA(T), that A · R < 0, and that a global line bundle L satisfies L · R < 0. Then L m≥0 f∗Lm is locally finitely generated. The relative Proj of a sufficiently divisible Veronese is a projective small contraction f+ : T+ → Z, where T+ is compact Kähler and globally strongly Q-factorial. The reflexive transform L+ is a rational line bundle, with a positive power equal to the relatively ample tautological bundle. The transformed boundary and the same b-nef datum define a gklt pair on T+, with relatively Kähler adjoint A+. This is the generalized flip, with the usual strict discrepancy increase at centres in either exceptional locus. Moreover, if t = (A · C)/(L · C) > 0 for an f-vertical curve C, then there is a unique η ∈ H1,1 BC(Z, R) such that A = t c1(L) + f∗ η, A+ = t c1(L+ ) + (f+ )∗ η. Every class on T has the corresponding forward transport with an actual exceptional-divisor correction. No assertion of surjectivity on Bott–Chern groups is required.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.19
candidates.name: Ordinary real boundaries
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.19 (Ordinary real boundaries).
candidates.statement: Let T be normal compact Kähler and globally Weil Q-factorial, with canonical sheaf a rational line bundle. Let B ≥ 0 be a real boundary with (T, B) klt. Assume the rational ordinary-step result of Proposition 3.48 for T and its subsequent models. Then every (KT + B)-negative extremal analytic ray has an ordinary step with projective contractions, compact Kähler models, and the expected opposite relative ample signs. Global Weil Q-factoriality is preserved; global strong Q-factoriality is preserved when imposed initially.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.25
candidates.name: Projective relative completion
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.25 (Projective relative completion).
candidates.statement: Let f : X → S be an already projective surjective morphism of normal compact Kähler spaces, with X smooth. Let (X, B + M) be an effective generalized klt pair with adjoint A, carried by a projective resolution p : W → X with smooth W, so that p∗ A = c1(KW ) + [BW ] + MW . Suppose that there are an actual real line bundle J ∈ Pic(X) ⊗ R and β ∈ H1,1 BC(S) such that A = c1(J) + f∗ β, N := p∗ J − KW − BW is nef and big over fp. Assume that J is pseudoeffective over S. Then there is a finite chosen A-negative projective program over S, with globally strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler working spaces, and a nonextracting endpoint Xm such that Jm ∼R g∗ H, Am = g∗ c1(H) + ρ∗ β  . 41 Here Jm is the actual real-line transform of J, g : Xm → Z is a projective connected-fibre morphism, ρ : Z → S is projective, and H is an actual real line bundle ample over S. Thus the class on Z in this formula is relatively Kähler over S. The generalized pair on Xm is gklt. On a common resolution the comparison with A is effective and exceptional over Xm, with strictly positive coefficient at the strict transform of every prime contracted from X.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.26
candidates.name: Semiampleness on an existing projective model
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.26 (Semiampleness on an existing projective model).
candidates.statement: Let f : T → S be a projective morphism of normal compact Kähler spaces with T globally strongly Q-factorial, and let J ∈ Pic(T) ⊗ R be nef over S. Suppose that on a finite Stein-compact cover satisfying condition (P), there are effective ordinary klt boundaries ∆ℓ, big over the base, such that KT + ∆ℓ ∼R J|TUℓ . Then J has the projective relative semiample contraction and actual descended ample real line of Proposition 3.25. In particular this applies to any already existing weak model of the fixed ordinary chart pairs in that proof; one need not run a new program for the adjoint in question.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.28
candidates.name: Ordinary projective Mori output
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.28 (Ordinary projective Mori output).
candidates.statement: Let f : X → S be an already projective surjective morphism of compact Kähler spaces, with X smooth. Let (X, B) be an effective ordinary real klt pair, and let D = KX + B. If D is not pseudoeffective over S, then its projective program over S, with scaling of a relatively ample actual real line N, terminates with a Mori fibre contraction. The initial scaling parameter is chosen so that D + TN is nef over S. The working spaces are globally strongly Q-factorial and compact Kähler, and the actual line comparisons and integral descent of Proposition 3.25 apply.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.30
candidates.name: Base presentations for projective contractions
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.30 (Base presentations for projective contractions).
candidates.statement: Let f : X → Z be a projective contraction between normal irreducible compact Kähler spaces. Suppose that (X, B + M) has globally modified-big total boundary and that A = [KX + B + MX] = f∗ γ, γ ∈ H1,1 BC(Z). There is an adjoint-preserving preparation as in Lemma 3.29, with multiplier ideal J1 ⊇ Jo, for which Ri f∗J1 = 0 (i > 0), f∗ON1 = OZ/(f∗J1), N1 = V (J1). (3.18) If N1 dominates Z, then f∗J1 = 0. Otherwise there are generalized data (Z, BZ + N), a projective carrier τ : T → Z with T smooth and compact Kähler, a real SNC structure divisor CT , and a Kähler class βT such that [KZ + BZ + NZ] = γ, τ∗ γ = [KT + CT ] + βT , NT = βT , BZ = τ∗CT ≥ 0, BZ + NZ is globally modified big. (3.19) The negative components of CT are τ-exceptional, and JZ := J (Z, BZ + N) = τ∗OT (−⌊CT ⌋) ⊇ f∗J1. (3.20) In particular the base data are gklt wherever f∗J1 is the unit ideal. If the source data are gklt, the base data are gklt. All adjoint identities are preserved by pullback to higher models.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.34
candidates.name: The contraction step over a lower-dimensional base
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.34 (The contraction step over a lower-dimensional base).
candidates.statement: Use the hypotheses and notation of Proposition 3.30. Suppose that A = f∗γ is nef and that its restriction to the original non-klt closed subspace No = V (Jo) is endowed with a Moishezon contraction. Put I = f∗J1, N∗ = V (I) ⊂ Z. Then γ|N∗ is endowed with a Moishezon contraction. If the prepared non-klt closed subspace N1 = V (J1) dominates Z, then γ and A are endowed with Moishezon contractions. Otherwise the generalized pair supplied on Z has a non-klt closed subspace endowed with the contraction defined by the restricted class of γ. In this latter case, if γ is nef and NQC and the assertion Cdim Z is available, then γ and A are endowed with Moishezon contractions.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.37
candidates.name: Uniform crepancy parameter; no termination assertion
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.37 (Uniform crepancy parameter; no termination assertion).
candidates.statement: Suppose additionally that the working spaces are d-dimensional klt spaces, that αi are nef, and that the ordinary canonical negative-ray length bound 0 < −KXi · C ≤ 2d is available. For a fixed real number t > 2d/δ, every negative extremal ray chosen in an existing (KXi + tαi)-program is αi-trivial. If the steps are projective ordinary canonical steps, Lemma 3.36 therefore applies inductively with this same value of t. If α0 is not big and α0 − c1(KX0 ) is big, then KXi + tαi remains non-pseudo-effective along these crepant steps. Consequently a terminating such program ends with a Mori fibre contraction. This corollary does not assert that the requisite contractions exist or that the program terminates.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.39
candidates.name: Stability under projective extraction
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.39 (Stability under projective extraction).
candidates.statement: Let r : Y → X be a projective bimero- morphic morphism of normal compact Kähler spaces with rational singularities. Suppose that Y is globally strongly Q-factorial and that X has the splitting property in the preceding lemma. Then Y has that property as well. More precisely, if E1, . . . , Es are the prime divisors exceptional for r, then H2 (Y, R) = r∗ H2 (X, R) ⊕ s M j=1 R[Ej], and the analogous statements hold over Q and in Bott–Chern cohomology.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.40
candidates.name: A uniform relative NQC bound
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.40 (A uniform relative NQC bound).
candidates.statement: Let f0 : U → Z be an already projective surjective morphism with connected fibres between smooth compact Kähler manifolds, and suppose that f∗ 0 : H0 (Z, Ω2 Z) −→ H0 (U, Ω2 U ) is an isomorphism. Let α0 be a nef class with an expression α0 = k X j=1 rjηj,0, rj > 0, ηj,0 ∈ H2 (U, Q), where ηj,0 has nonnegative degree on every curve vertical over Z. Let D0 = KU + ∆U + MU be a generalized klt adjoint. Consider its projective relative program for D0 + aα0, under the projective local ordinary reduction described in the proof of Lemma 3.47. 60 If α0 = 0, triviality is immediate. Otherwise there are positive integers mj, chosen once on U, and a number δ = min j rj mj > 0 such that, for aδ > 2 dim U, the entire relative program is α0-trivial. The same number a works at every step.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.46
candidates.name: Any lower-dimensional good model suffices
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.46 (Any lower-dimensional good model suffices).
candidates.statement: Suppose the initial relative program has the data in Lemma 3.42. Assume in addition that its class αV is nef and agrees with µ∗α on a common resolution, and that there is an already projective connected-fibre morphism g : V → S with αV = g∗ αS, DV = g∗ DS. Suppose there is a projective small modification s : Sq → S such that Sq is globally Weil Q-factorial; the identity is allowed. Assume that the lower-dimensional adjoint s∗DS has a good model: there are a normal compact Kähler space Sm, a common projective resolution p : W → Sq, q : W → Sm, and a nef semiample class Dm such that p∗ s∗ DS = q∗ Dm + [E], E ≥ 0, E is q-exceptional. Then α is semiample on X. If the contraction defining semiampleness of Dm is Moishezon, the resulting contraction of α is Moishezon as well. In particular, it is unnecessary to lift a program on S to V , or to require that a chosen program producing Sm preserve αS at every intermediate step.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.48
candidates.name: A negative ray with an actual detector
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.48 (A negative ray with an actual detector).
candidates.statement: Assume Bd. Let A be a gklt adjoint in dimension at most d on a globally strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler space, with globally nef carrier data. Let R be an A-negative extremal ray of the full analytic cone. If an actual global rational line L has L · R < 0, the ray has a projective contraction; a small contraction has its detected flip. The working models retain the strong factoriality and compact Kähler properties. In particular this applies to an ordinary rational adjoint A = c1(KX + B) with detector KX + B, and to ordinary real boundaries by Proposition 3.19.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.55
candidates.name: The restricted package in every dimension
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.55 (The restricted package in every dimension).
candidates.statement: The assertions Bd, Cd, Md and Fd hold in every finite dimension, for the globally nef carrier data and globally modified-big 77 boundary traces specified above. All birational steps used to prove them are detected steps or belong to an already-projective relative construction with the stated relative-line algebraicity. A general semiample morphism is asserted to be Moishezon; projectivity is asserted only when the construction provides an actual relatively ample line.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.56
candidates.name: Finite positive parts of detected scalings
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.56 (Finite positive parts of detected scalings).
candidates.statement: Let a gklt adjoint with globally nef carrier data be run with scaling of the trace of a Kähler class on a fixed smooth carrier. Suppose that every chosen negative analytic ray has an actual global rational line detector and that the total boundary trace on each positive scaling segment is globally modified big. Every segment whose scaling parameters lie in a fixed interval [ε, T], with ε > 0, is finite. If the driving adjoint is not pseudo-effective, the scaling terminates with a Mori fibre space.

candidates.label: Theorem 4.1
candidates.name: Generation on the reduced boundary
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.1 (Generation on the reduced boundary).
candidates.statement: Assume Gj for every 0 ≤ j < n. Let (V, B) be a normal irreducible compact Kähler dlt n-fold with effective rational boundary B. Suppose that V is globally Q-factorial, that (V, B) satisfies the lc-strata resolution convention of Definition 3.1, and that the actual Q-Cartier adjoint J = KV + B is analytically nef. Then the restriction of an actual positive Cartier multiple of J to the whole reduced space S = ⌊B⌋ is globally generated.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.6
candidates.name: Finite image of self-arrows
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.6 (Finite image of self-arrows).
candidates.statement: Let Z be a boundary stratum with CZ vertical. For all sufficiently large divisible k, the self-arrows of Z have finite image on H0(Z, Lk Z).

candidates.label: Proposition 4.7
candidates.name: A polarized top-form scalar
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.7 (A polarized top-form scalar).
candidates.statement: Let U be a smooth connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension d < n, and let g : U 99K U be bimeromorphic. Suppose that on a common smooth resolution the two pullbacks of some Kähler class on U differ by an element of NSR. If 0 ̸= α ∈ H0(U, KU ) and g∗α = µα, then µ is a root of unity.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.11
candidates.name: Generating tuples
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.11 (Generating tuples).
candidates.statement: There is a degree k > 0 and a compatible invariant generating system of tuples through dimension n − 1.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.name: The rank-one case
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1 (The rank-one case).
candidates.statement: Assume Assumption 1.1. Fix n > 0 and assume Gd for every d < n. Let X be a smooth connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension n, let B be a rational SNC boundary, and suppose that J = KX + B is pseudo-effective. Suppose there are smooth compact Kähler manifolds e X, W, a modification π : e X → X, and a proper surjective holomorphic map g : e X → W with connected fibers such that 0 < k := dim W < n, W is projective or a(W) = 0. Assume that e B = π−1 ∗ B + Exc(π)red has SNC support and that, on a very general smooth fiber F of g, κ(F, KF + e BF ) = 0. 98 Then (X, B) satisfies Gn.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.5
candidates.name: A conditional generalized program
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.5 (A conditional generalized program).
candidates.statement: Assume Assumption 1.1. Let (V, B+M) be a projective generalized dlt rational pair, where V is Q-factorial, B ≥ 0, and the nef b-divisor M is determined by a nef rational Cartier divisor on a projective birational model. Put D = KV +B+MV . 103 There is a choice of D-MMP with ample scaling which terminates. If D is pseudo-effective, its endpoint Vm has nef adjoint Dm. If D is not pseudo-effective, its endpoint has a Mori fiber contraction to a projective variety of smaller dimension. The birational steps and their endpoints stay Q-factorial generalized dlt, and the forward birational map extracts no divisors. In the pseudo-effective case, on a common resolution one has an actual rational divisor identity u∗ D = v∗ Dm + F, F ≥ 0 and v-exceptional.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.9
candidates.name: Generation from a big nef base line
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.9 (Generation from a big nef base line).
candidates.statement: Assume Gd for d < n. Let (Z, ∆Z) be a globally Q-factorial dlt compact Kähler pair of dimension n satisfying the resolution condition of Definition 3.1, with effective rational boundary and analytically nef adjoint L = KZ + ∆Z. Suppose there are a smooth compact Kähler manifold U, a projective resolution r : U → Z, a proper surjection f : U → Y to a normal projective variety, and a big nef rational line HY on Y such that r∗ L ∼Q f∗ HY (5.15) as actual rational lines. Then L is semiample.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.1.
candidates.statement: Let X be a smooth connected compact Kähler manifold. Suppose that a(X) = 0 and that no positive-dimensional proper compact analytic subvariety passes through a very general point of X. Then K⊗m X has a nonzero meromorphic section for some integer m > 0.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.7
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.7.
candidates.statement: Let Y be a smooth compact Kähler manifold and E a holomorphic vector bundle of rank at least two. Write πE : PY (E) → Y and ζE = c1(OP(E)(1)). Suppose that a real class D on Y satisfies c1(H) ≤ kD whenever 0 ̸= H −→ E⊗k for a line bundle H and integer k ≥ 0. For a real class A on Y and a real number b ≥ 0, π∗ EA + bζE ≥ 0 =⇒ A + bD ≥ 0. (6.18)

candidates.label: Theorem 7.1
candidates.name: Signed rigidity
candidates.heading: Theorem 7.1 (Signed rigidity).
candidates.statement: Let (X, D) be a dlt pair on a normal irreducible compact Kähler space, and suppose that the pair has the resolution property of Definition 3.1. Suppose also that X is globally Q-factorial, that a(X) = 0, that X is simple, and that D = Ps i=1 Di is reduced. Put L = KX + D, and assume the following. (i) The rational line L is analytically nef and has an actual rational linear equivalence L ∼Q G = s X i=1 aiDi, ai ∈ Q. (ii) For some real c > 0, the pullback of the class {L − cD} to a projective resolution with smooth compact Kähler source is pseudo-effective. (iii) The rational holomorphic line L|D is semiample on the whole reduced analytic space D: some Cartier multiple is generated at every point of D. Then L is torsion. More precisely, for some positive integer q, the holomorphic line OX(qL) is isomorphic to OX.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.5
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.5.
candidates.statement: Let q : V → Y be a holomorphic map of complex manifolds, submersive near a reduced closed analytic subspace i : H ,→ V of pure dimension d and codimension c0 > 0. Suppose h = q|H is proper. Assume that locally H is an SNC divisor in a smooth submanifold of codimension c0 − 1, and that a reduced divisor A is simultaneously SNC and transverse to those support equations. Assume that the components Hi and Aj near H have finite global smooth 141 indexing, and that every closed stratum HI ∩ AJ , with I ̸= ∅, is smooth and proper over Y and carries a global relative Kähler form. Empty or disconnected strata are allowed. Here HI = T i∈I Hi and AJ = T j∈J Aj, with A∅ = V. Use right D-modules and finite-pole local cohomology, and put KA = Hc0 [H](ωV)(∗A). Its order filtration is generated from F0KA = i∗ωH(A), with Fp = 0 for p < 0. For Mj = Hjq+KA, the filtered direct image is strict at every level, and Mj has a finite filtration by submodules, strict for F, whose quotients are polarizable real pure Hodge modules. In particular, F0Mj = Rj h∗ωH(A) ,−→ Mj , FpMj = 0 (p < 0). (7.11) Define the symbol morphism σ : F0Mj ⊗ TY −→ grF 1 Mj , σ(m ⊗ ξ) = [mξ]. If Y is smooth projective, then for every ample line N on Y , HomOY (N, ker σ) = 0. (7.12) This includes any coherent torsion in the kernel.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.6
candidates.name: All finite lifting orders
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.6 (All finite lifting orders).
candidates.statement: For every root chart, every j ∈ Z, and every k ≥ 1, the map of sheaves of complex vector spaces on U g∗Tj,k+1 −→ g∗Tj,k (7.16) is surjective. The assertion holds on every parameter germ, including germs supported at special parameters.

manuscripts.title: Uniform indices for semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: For every integer d ≥ 4 and every finite set Φ ⊂ [0, 1] ∩ Q, there is an integer a(d, Φ) > 0 with the following property. Let (X, B) be a connected projective equidimensional semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pair of dimension d over k, with every nonzero coefficient of B in Φ. Then a(d, Φ)(KX + B) is Cartier, OX (︁ a(d, Φ)(KX + B) )︁ ≃ OX.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.2
candidates.name: Normal index theorem [36, Theorem 1.2]
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.2 (Normal index theorem [36, Theorem 1.2]).
candidates.statement: For every integer d ≥ 0 and every rational set I ⊂ [0, 1] satisfying the descending chain condition, there is an integer alc(d, I) > 0 such that every normal projective integral lc pair (X, ∆) of dimension d, with coefficients in I and KX + ∆ ∼Q 0, satisfies alc(d, I)(KX + ∆) ∼ 0.

candidates.name: Good minimal models [33, Theorem 11.1]
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.3 (Good minimal models [33, Theorem 11.1]).
candidates.statement: A projective lc pair over C with effective rational boundary and pseudo-effective log canonical divisor has a good log minimal model. In particular its adjoint is nonvanishing and its transform on the good model is semiample.
candidates.cited_by: Theorem 2.3 (Good minimal models [33, Theorem 11.1]).

candidates.label: Proposition 2.4
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.4.
candidates.statement: Fix n. Let h : V → Y be a contraction over C, where V is klt of dimension n, KV ∼Q 0, and 0 < b = dim Y < n. Suppose that a smooth projective resolution of Y is rationally connected. Then Y is isomorphic in codimension one to a normal projective variety ˆ︁ Y in a bounded family depending only on n. In particular ˆ︁ Y has a very ample Cartier divisor H for which Hb ≤ Cn, |Kˆ︁ Y · Hb−1 | ≤ Cn. (2.2) The canonical intersection is the degree of the canonical Weil divisor on a general complete- intersection curve in the smooth locus.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.1.
candidates.statement: For every integer n ≥ 2 there is a constant Rn with the following property. Let T be a projective Q-factorial terminal complex n-fold with KT ∼ 0. Suppose that a smooth projective resolution U has h1(U, OU ) = 0, and that every positive-dimensional rational image of T of dimension less than n has a rationally connected smooth projective resolution. Then r(T) = dimQ T(U) ≤ Rn.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.1
candidates.name: Uniform klt character exponent
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.1 (Uniform klt character exponent).
candidates.statement: For integers n ≥ 0 and m ≥ 1, there is an integer L(n, m) > 0 with the following property. Let (X, ∆) be an integral projective klt n-fold pair, with ∆ ≥ 0 and m(KX + ∆) ∼ 0 as an integral principal divisor. Choose a rational m-canonical form θ with Div(θ) = −m∆. manuscripts.title: Conditional good minimal models for compact Kähler fourfolds

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.name: Conditional good minimal models
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1 (Conditional good minimal models).
candidates.statement: Assume Assumptions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4. Let X be a normal connected compact Kähler fourfold, and let B be an effective rational Weil divisor. Suppose that (X, B) is klt, that its actual adjoint D = KX + B is Q-Cartier and analytically pseudo-effective, and that X is globally strongly Q-factorial in the sense of Definition 2.1. Then there are a normal connected globally strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold Y and a bimeromorphic map ϕ : X 99K Y such that: (i) ϕ extracts no prime divisor, and BY = ϕ∗B; (ii) (Y, BY ) is klt and its actual adjoint DY = KY + BY is Q-Cartier and analytically nef; (iii) a(E; Y, BY ) ≥ a(E; X, B) for every prime divisor over the models, with strict inequality for each prime on X contracted by ϕ; (iv) for some m > 0, the Cartier line bundle OY (mDY ) is globally generated.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.name: Nonvanishing on the nef endpoint
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2 (Nonvanishing on the nef endpoint).
candidates.statement: Under Assumptions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4, let (Y, ∆) be an ordinary klt pair on a normal connected globally strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold. If ∆ is effective and rational and the actual Q-Cartier adjoint J = KY + ∆ is analytically nef, then κ(Y, J) ≥ 0.

manuscripts.title: Projective-space bases of Lagrangian fibrations

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let n ≥ 1, and let X be a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold of dimension 2n, with symplectic form σ. Suppose that f : X −→ B is a projective surjective holomorphic morphism with connected fibers, where B is a normal projective variety of dimension n. Assume that every irreducible component of every fiber has dimension n and that the restriction of σ to its smooth locus is zero. Then B is isomorphic to Pn C.

The base is Q-factorial and klt, has Picard number one, and −KB is ample as a Q-Cartier divisor. A smooth fiber is an abelian variety after choosing an origin. 5 2. There are reflexive identifications Rj f∗OX ≃ Ω [j] B . For every integral Weil divisor A ample as a Q-divisor, Hi  B, (Ω [j] B ⊗ OB(A))∗∗  = 0 (i > 0, j > 0). The reflexivity assertion also applies locally to the projective equidimensional fibrations with connected fibers, smooth source Z satisfying ωZ ≃ OZ, and normal Cohen–Macaulay Q-Gorenstein target that occur below. 3. The rational intersection cohomology of B has the Betti numbers of Pn, and the restriction of H2(X, Q) to a smooth fiber has one-dimensional image. 4. If B is smooth, then B ≃ Pn.

If a holomorphic line bundle L satisfies c1(L) ̸= 0, c1(L) ∈ KY , qY (c1(L)) = 0, then a positive tensor power of L is generated by its global sections. Its associated map with connected fibers has a normal projective base of dimension m. Every component of every fiber has dimension m and is Lagrangian.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.2
candidates.name: Rational smoothness
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.2 (Rational smoothness).
candidates.statement: The space B is an oriented rational homology manifold of real dimension 2n. Its rational intersection complex is QB[n]. Consequently its ordinary rational cohomology has the Betti numbers of Pn. The local rational homology- manifold assertion holds for every normal germ finitely dominated by a smooth germ, in particular for the maximal charts constructed below.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3
candidates.name: Maximal quasi-étale charts and normalized source charts
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.3 (Maximal quasi-étale charts and normalized source charts).
candidates.statement: Every pointed germ (B, b) has a connected finite normal Galois quasi-étale cover (C, c) which dominates every connected finite quasi-étale cover of that germ. The chart (C, c) is klt, is finitely dominated by a smooth germ, and has no nontrivial connected finite quasi-étale cover. The finite diagrams can be defined over an algebraic étale neighborhood of b. More generally, let U → B be an integral separated étale algebraic neighborhood and let π : C → U be an integral finite normal quasi-étale cover. Put XU = X ×B U. The base change XU ×U C has a unique irreducible component dominating C; let Z be its normalization and h : Z → C its structure map. Then h is projective and equidimensional of relative dimension n, has connected fibers, and satisfies h∗OZ = OC. The finite map p : Z → XU is étale. Consequently Z is smooth, the pullback of the symplectic form on X is symplectic on Z, its canonical bundle is trivial, and the fibers of h are Lagrangian. If π is Galois with group Γ, then p is a Γ-torsor. Ordinary étale base change on C preserves projectivity, equidimensionality, connected fibers, the equality h∗OZ = OC, and the smooth symplectic source. The torsor in the statement belongs to the original finite chart.

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.6 (The residual tensor group).

For a choice of ω, tensor reconstruction identifies it with RepC(G), where G = Aut⊗ (ω) is a reductive algebraic subgroup of GL(Vfib) and Vfib = ω(V ). This representation is faithful and has dimension n.

candidates.statement: Let d = minb∈B s(b). If d = n, every germ of B is a quotient singularity. Otherwise the minimum locus is a nonempty closed algebraic subset. Each of its connected components S0 is irreducible, normal and projective of dimension d. There are finitely many normal finite Galois quasi-étale charts Vα → Bα, with deck groups Γα and with Bα → B separated and étale, covering S0. They are maximal at every point over S0. 2. Normalized main overlaps give an étale groupoid along the reduced inverse images Sα ⊂ Vα. Its quotient is the stack S of Proposition 4.3. Writing I for the marked ideal on the object charts, the same finite diagrams define, for every k ≥ 1, a proper separated Deligne– Mumford stack Sk, with S1 = S. Its coarse space is finite over B and projective. 3. A finite family of étale refinements of the object charts covers their closed strata and has the marked-product presentations of Lemma 4.4. All transition maps come from the normalized ambient overlaps and preserve I exactly. Their restrictions are consequently compatible for all powers Ik. 4. The normalized source charts give ordinary pullback and descent of coherent sheaves on any Sk to coherent sheaves on X supported over S0. These assertions are encoded by finitely many algebraic schemes, morphisms, ideals and identities. In particular they can be spread simultaneously before choosing any order of Frobenius pullback.

candidates.statement: If a nonprojective compact irreducible hyperkähler manifold Z of complex dimension 2n contains a holomorphic Lagrangian complex torus S, then its algebraic dimension is n and it has a holomorphic algebraic reduction Z → B which is a Lagrangian fibration with S as a fiber. references: [15] Daniel Greb, Christian Lehn, and Sönke Rollenske. Lagrangian fibrations on hyperkähler manifolds—on a question of Beauville. Annales scientifiques de l’École normale supérieure, 46(3):375–403, 2013.

manuscripts.title: Every complex K3 surface is Oka

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let X be a complex K3 surface, with any smooth Hermitian distance dX. For every integer m ≥ 1, every nonempty compact convex set K ⊂ Cm, every open neighborhood U of K, every holomorphic map f : U → X, and every ϵ > 0, there exists a holomorphic map F : Cm → X such that sup z∈K dX(F(z), f(z)) < ϵ.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2.
candidates.statement: Let S be a complex K3 surface. For every x ∈ S and every nonzero vector v ∈ TxS, there is a holomorphic immersion f : C → S such that f(0) = x, f′ (0) = v, f(C) = S, where closure is taken in the ordinary complex topology. If S is projective, then f(C) is Zariski dense.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.2
candidates.name: Two complete directions
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.2 (Two complete directions).
candidates.statement: Suppose there are holomorphic maps σ1 : C × ∆b −→ X, σ2 : ∆b × C −→ X which are locally biholomorphic at (0, 0) and satisfy σ1(z, 0) = σ2(z, 0) for small z. If σ2 is locally biholomorphic at (0, c), then L holds at x = σ2(0, c). The same conclusion holds for a sequence of pairs whose long coordinate domains are discs of radii tending to infinity, whose bounded-coordinate radii are bounded below, and whose maps converge near (0, 0) and, for the second map, near (0, c) to the above nondegenerate germs. Exact axis agreement is required for every pair. In this version x is the value of the limiting second germ at (0, c).

candidates.label: Proposition 2.9
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.9.
candidates.statement: Let K be a closed circular disc of radius r, or a closed circular annulus with outer radius r, and let f be holomorphic near K × P, where P is a closed polydisc. Suppose that for every ζ on the outer circle there is a coordinate witness neighborhood Vζ for L containing f({ζ} × P). For every R > r and P0 ⋐ int P, one can approximate f uniformly on K × P0 by a map holomorphic near the enlarged disc, respectively annulus with the same inner radius and outer radius R, times P0.

candidates.label: Corollary 2.10
candidates.name: Propagation across a small disc
candidates.heading: Corollary 2.10 (Propagation across a small disc).
candidates.statement: Suppose a coordinate neighborhood contains a closed affine complex-line disc centered at x, with its boundary in the open locus where L holds. 11 Then L holds at x. In particular, if the complement of that locus is contained locally in a proper analytic subset, L holds everywhere.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.1.
candidates.statement: Let Y be a complex surface with a complete compatible distance. If the local operation L holds at every point of Y , then Y has the convex approximation property in every source dimension.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.4
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.4.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1.

candidates.statement: Every projective complex K3 surface and every complex Enriques surface is elliptic in Gromov’s sense.

candidates.statement: Given W > 0 and R0 > 0, there is a torsion-free principal congruence subgroup Γ0, normalized by σ, with the following properties. (2) The injectivity radius of Γ0\B is greater than R0. (3) In the ball of radius R0 about o, the arrangement is exactly D restricted to that ball. The analogous assertion holds in every Γ0-translate of this ball. All these conclusions concerning the lifted arrangement remain valid on any subsequent finite cover of Γ0\B, provided one uses the full inverse image of the arrangement.
